text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- An international exercise, Baltic Challenge, under the auspices of NATO's Partnership for Peace programme, began at the Estonian port of Paldiski on Monday.
- The general assembly of Underrepresented Nations begins in the southern Estonian lakeside resort of Otepaa.
- The Security Police are investigating the sale of KGB files on two members of parliament.

- The number of crimes rose by 16.7 percent in Estonia in the first six months of this year compared to the same period last year. Robberies and burglaries continue to grow while more serious offenses like murders and rapes have decreased slightly.
- Ex-prime minister Tiit Vahi warns in an interview against attempts to change the economic policies that have brought success to Estonia.
- West Energy Net was separated from Estonian Energy to achieve better economic results, the economy ministry said.
